crop.notes: Whole article: headline 'Tom Allen Was Worth Only $279', deck, the boxed list of possessions and the full body. The top of the clipping includes the lower part of an unrelated portrait of Senator Charles A. Smith.

ocr.notes: The body text is mostly right. The headline is missing and most of the amounts in the possessions box are garbled; the image shows them clearly (e.g. whisky $18.00, cup and shade $25.00, horse and harness $80.00, other effects $102.15, total $279.80).

summary.suggested: The St. Louis Post-Dispatch reported that Public Administrator Garrard Strode's inventory of Tom Allen's estate, filed in probate court, valued it at only $279.80, including his champion's cup at $25.

metadata.notes: Masthead reads 'St. Louis Post-Dispatch, Tuesday Evening, July 28, 1903', front page.

facts.fact: Public Administrator Garrard Strode filed the inventory and appraisal of Allen's estate in probate court; it valued everything at $279.80
The inventory listed Allen's champion's cup and shade at $25, a horse and harness at $80, an old piano and stool at $11, and $11 cash from John Murphy
After Allen's death the Champion's Rest fell into other hands, and a will was produced leaving his property to his two married daughters, one in St. Louis and one in England

notes: The will described here (to the two daughters) matches the index entry 'Another article says Allen left everything to his two daughters' (id 000); it conflicts with the Globe-Democrat of the next day (1012), which says the will left $10 to each daughter and the rest to Tillie Hartgrove. The inventory does not include the mallet Allen used to rap for order at his concerts.
